clue.text: Criterion magistrates have to observe

parts.note: the magistrates sitting in court are collectively the bench
to mark something is to notice or observe it

explanation.surface: Magistrates must keep an eye on some standard of judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a standard or yardstick against which other things are measured.

clue.text: Beefy nobleman?

parts.note: a hefty lord in the surface, but a double sirloin joint of beef carries the title of a peer

explanation.surface: A burly aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'baron of beef' is a large butcher's joint of two sirloins left joined at the backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint of meat shares its name with the lowest rank of the peerage, hence the beefy title.

clue.text: Curious about mature climbing flowers

indicators.note: the word for curious goes around the other piece

parts.note: curious, prying, means nosy

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word for mature is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A nosy person wonders about some ageing climbing plants.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads upwards, so the reversed EGA is what 'about' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy or bunch of fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Listen to male cat held up in anguish

parts.note: to listen to is to hear

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means the word for the animal is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Hearing a tomcat stuck up a tree causes distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns CAT into TAC; the charade runs HEAR, TAC, HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is deep sorrow or emotional distress, a kind of mental anguish.

clue.text: Enunciated clearly, being' well-connected?

definitions.meaning: jointed, made of linked sections like a lorry with a trailer

explanation.surface: Speaking crisply because one has good social links.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'being' is a print slip; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulated lorry is jointed, its parts connected, while articulate speech is clear and distinct.

clue.text: Sort of beer available in King's Head, say

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from King's

parts.note: say, for example, is abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A pub called the King's Head serves a particular kind of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head looks like a pub name, but 'Head' picks the K of King's.
explanation.definitionFit: Keg beer is beer served pressurised from a metal cask, a type of draught.

clue.text: Loud organ let fly

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a lung is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A loud church organ gave full blast.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is to throw something hard, which is what you have done when you have hurled it.

clue.text: Miss Poste's plants

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Stella Gibbons's novel Cold Comfort Farm, whose first name is wanted
the plant life of a region, collectively

explanation.surface: A woman's houseplants.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold Comfort Farm is a much-loved 1932 English comic novel whose heroine is Miss Poste.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term for the vegetation of an area is also a woman's given name.

clue.text: Intrude somehow without being heard

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of intrude are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone barges in silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without being heard' suggests stealth, but it means a case not yet heard in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that has not been tried in court has not been heard by a judge.

clue.text: Plant, or birch

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold, so golden
a birch is a rod for beating

explanation.surface: A choice between a plant and a birch tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word, but in heraldry it is gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a tall garden plant with yellow flower spikes.

clue.text: Missing diva's opening, singer has to begin again

indicators.note: missing says a letter is lost from the word for the singer

parts.note: the redstart is a songbird, so a singer

indicators.note: the opening of the word diva is its first letter

explanation.surface: A diva misses her entrance and the singer must start over.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer is not the diva but a bird, the redstart; dropping D gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to start once more, beginning a second time.

clue.text: Girl about 50 beyond limit comes to a sort of stop

indicators.note: the word for girl goes around the other pieces

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
OTT, over the top, means beyond reasonable limits

explanation.surface: A girl pushing fifty goes too far and finally halts.
explanation.walkthrough: A glottal stop is the catch in the throat replacing a T in some accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A glottal stop is a consonant made by closing the vocal cords, so the adjective names a kind of stop.

clue.text: The recurrent Fall of Man, say

definitions.text: The recurrent Fall of Man, say

parts.words: The recurrent Fall of Man, say
parts.note: not the biblical fall but darkness falling over everyone again each day

explanation.surface: Humanity's repeated fall from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall of Man' suggests Adam and Eve; the thing that falls on mankind daily is darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness falls every evening, a daily recurrence over all humankind.

clue.text: Players a team has to discard

parts.note: the players in a play are its cast
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Actors and a sports team must get rid of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something away as no longer wanted is to discard it.

clue.text: Protest about time taken to clean up the lounge

indicators.note: the word for protest goes around the letter for time

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest occupation
to groom is to clean and tidy

explanation.surface: Demonstrators take time out to tidy the lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting-room is the living room or front room of a house.

clue.text: Girl with plenty of dates

definitions.meaning: a month with thirty-one days on the calendar

explanation.surface: A popular girl with many romantic engagements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dates' suggests romance, but means days of the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth month has thirty-one days, and is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Sensational performance setting off dome alarm

indicators.note: setting off an alarm, read as setting its letters off in a new order

explanation.surface: A dramatic show sets off a cathedral dome's alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a play with exaggerated, sensational events and emotions.

clue.text: Telephone to authorise instruction to start meeting

parts.note: to telephone is to call
to order something is to authorise it to be done

explanation.surface: Ring up for permission to begin the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman calls a meeting to order, directing it to begin its formal business.

clue.text: To discard, one 'throws this on the table

definitions.text: To discard, one 'throws this on the table

parts.words: To discard, one 'throws this on the table
parts.note: discarding means throwing something off a ship's side, and a card player discarding throws a card over onto the board

explanation.surface: A card player's discard lands on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe before 'throws' is a print slip. Throwing something over the ship's side is discarding it.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing items off a ship into the sea is the classic way to get rid of them.

clue.text: Plant that's least restrained and widespread

parts.note: loosest means least tightly bound
rife means common or widespread

explanation.surface: A plant that grows freely and abundantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosestrife is a waterside plant, purple or yellow flowered.

clue.text: Unfinished at the time of departure

definitions.meaning: read as two words, at the moment of leaving

explanation.surface: Still in progress when leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still in progress continues; split, the word says at the point of leaving.

clue.text: In a sorry state, having failed to rise

definitions.meaning: said of bread or cake that stays heavy and flat

explanation.surface: Miserable after a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad means unhappy, and a sad cake is one that sank in the oven.

clue.text: This sort of verse isn't free, in the main.

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for the main

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea

indicators.note: free here means loose, letting the letters of isn't move

explanation.surface: This poem is not free verse and is about the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' suggests free verse, the very thing this strict form is not; here it signals the shuffle to STIN, and 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is a strict verse form of six six-line stanzas with repeated end words.

clue.text: Magistrate's given a time to execute key cut-throat

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice
to do a task is to execute it
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A magistrate is given a date to execute a murderous plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice and Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eat-dog world is ruthlessly competitive, a cut-throat one.

clue.text: Visibly prepared to eat feast

definitions.meaning: the Christian love feast of the early church

explanation.surface: Ready to tuck into a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping open-mouthed looks like readiness to eat; the Greek love feast shares the spelling.

clue.text: Woman employed to clean

definitions.meaning: a dialect term of abuse for a woman

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a twig broom, and also a scornful Scots word for a woman.

clue.text: Sort of meat found in chop

definitions.meaning: to cut into very small pieces

explanation.surface: A kind of meat inside a pork chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced beef is ground meat, and to mince is to chop finely.

clue.text: A major worry for David's wife

parts.note: big means major or large
to ail is to trouble or worry

explanation.surface: A great concern for the king's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Abigail was one of King David's wives in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Abigail married King David after the death of Nabal.

clue.text: Wreath that's left over

indicators.note: over says the abbreviation for that is should be turned around

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A wreath remains after the funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left over' reads as remaining, but 'left' is L and 'over' turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: Sort of reception in which you may have to stand

definitions.text: Sort of reception in which you may have to stand

parts.words: Sort of reception in which you may have to stand
parts.note: not a drinks party with no chairs, but an audience on its feet applauding

explanation.surface: A party with standing room only.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'standing' version of this reception is an audience rising to applaud.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing ovation is an enthusiastic welcome in which the crowd rises to clap.

clue.text: Butcher not starting to provide fish

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the word for butcher is dropped

parts.note: to butcher a job is to mangle it

explanation.surface: A butcher who won't start the day supplies fish instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like a shopkeeper but is a verb, to mangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line.

clue.text: Beset 'by time scramble, news channels become most pressing

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
scramble says the letters of time are mixed up

parts.note: the media are the channels that carry news

explanation.surface: Short of time, broadcasters scramble to cover the most urgent story.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe before 'by' is a print slip. 'scramble' gives IMTE, split so that 'Beset by' wraps it round the news channels.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immediate demands attention first, being the most urgent.
